name: Benthic Macroinvertebrates
protocol_question: Turn over 3 riverbed stones in riffle areas. What macroinvertebrate organisms do you observe?
citizen_question: Turn over 3 riverbed stones in riffle areas. What macroinvertebrate organisms do you observe? Look for Mayfly, Stonefly, or Caddisfly larvae.
visual_anchor_guide: Look for Mayfly, Stonefly, or Caddisfly larvae under stones (sensitive) vs. aquatic worms/leeches (tolerant).

states.label: Tolerant taxa only (Midges, Leeches, Aquatic Worms)

lab_guidance: Optional: preserve specimens for lab confirmation.
citation: Schmeller, D., Calapez, A.R., Silva, J.P., Norte, A.C., Serra, S.R.Q., Dias, M., Silva, G.T., Bouchali, R., Loyau, A., Almeida, S.F.P., Schmitt, R., Chen, A., Ramos, J.A., Feio, M.J. (2026). OneAquaHealth Key Indicators Factsheets Collection. Zenodo. doi:10.5281/zenodo.20345207
why_this_matters: Healthy macroinvertebrate communities indicate clean water and functioning ecological processes, which are directly linked to human and animal health by supporting safe drinking water sources, fisheries and disease-limiting environments.
why_this_matters_source: Importance of indicator — II. Benthic Macroinvertebrates (factsheet_text.txt)

name: Birds
protocol_question: Conduct a 10-minute visual/auditory observation along a 100m stream transect. What riverine birds are present?
citizen_question: Conduct a 10-minute visual/auditory observation along a 100m stream transect. What riverine birds are present? Listen for Kingfishers, Dippers, or Grey Wagtails.
visual_anchor_guide: Listen and observe for Kingfishers, Dippers, or Grey Wagtails along the bank using the Merlin Mobile App guide.

states.label: Multiple riverine bird species observed active along transect
Single riverine species or generalist birds observed
No avian activity recorded during 10-minute window

lab_guidance: Optional: photograph birds for expert confirmation.
citation: Schmeller, D., Calapez, A.R., Silva, J.P., Norte, A.C., Serra, S.R.Q., Dias, M., Silva, G.T., Bouchali, R., Loyau, A., Almeida, S.F.P., Schmitt, R., Chen, A., Ramos, J.A., Feio, M.J. (2026). OneAquaHealth Key Indicators Factsheets Collection. Zenodo. doi:10.5281/zenodo.20345207
why_this_matters: The number of insectivorous bird species between areas differing in degree of urbanisation, and across habitat changes evaluated in long-term monitoring, will elucidate about the resilience of the ecosystem regarding pest control (disease vector mosquitoes, plant pests, etc), and the quality of cultural services that contribute to human well-being.

name: Invasive Alien Plants of the Riparian Corridor
protocol_question: Examine both stream banks along a 50m stretch. Do you see invasive plant coverage?
citizen_question: Examine both stream banks along a 50m stretch. Do you see invasive plant coverage? Check for Japanese Knotweed, Himalayan Balsam, or Giant Hogweed.
visual_anchor_guide: Check for Japanese Knotweed, Himalayan Balsam, or Giant Hogweed patches choking native vegetation.

states.label: No invasive alien plant species observed
Isolated patches along the riparian margin
Dense, widespread coverage dominating stream banks

lab_guidance: Optional: collect specimens for lab identification.
citation: Schmeller, D., Calapez, A.R., Silva, J.P., Norte, A.C., Serra, S.R.Q., Dias, M., Silva, G.T., Bouchali, R., Loyau, A., Almeida, S.F.P., Schmitt, R., Chen, A., Ramos, J.A., Feio, M.J. (2026). OneAquaHealth Key Indicators Factsheets Collection. Zenodo. doi:10.5281/zenodo.20345207
why_this_matters: In terms of health impacts, AIPs, particularly angiosperms, are frequently associated with the production of allergenic pollen and toxic compounds, which can cause wounds, skin irritation, allergic reactions and poisoning. Additionally, IAPs may act as mediators of disease vectors (e.g., dipteran vectors, ticks) and allow the occurrence and proliferation of vector-borne diseases.
why_this_matters_source: Importance of indicator — XI. Invasive Alien Plants of the riparian corridor (factsheet_text.txt)

name: Fecal Coliforms
protocol_question: Collect a 250mL water sample in a sterile container for laboratory membrane filtration (CFU/100mL).
citizen_question: Collect a 250mL water sample in a sterile container for laboratory membrane filtration (CFU/100mL).
visual_anchor_guide: Collect water sample in sterile container. Filter on selective growth medium. Incubate at warm temperatures. Count colonies as CFU/100mL.
lab_guidance: Requires membrane filtration or enzyme-substrate culture testing in an accredited laboratory (Method 9222 / ISO 9308-1). Cannot be evaluated visually in the field.
citation: Schmeller, D., Calapez, A.R., Silva, J.P., Norte, A.C., Serra, S.R.Q., Dias, M., Silva, G.T., Bouchali, R., Loyau, A., Almeida, S.F.P., Schmitt, R., Chen, A., Ramos, J.A., Feio, M.J. (2026). OneAquaHealth Key Indicators Factsheets Collection. Zenodo. doi:10.5281/zenodo.20345207
why_this_matters: Their presence suggests inputs from human or animal waste and therefore a potential exposure to enteric pathogens including pathogenic bacteria, and parasites. This makes them a reliable early warning signal for the potential presence of harmful pathogens such as E. coli O157, Salmonella, or viruses (e.g. norovirus causing gastroenteritis) and parasites associated with gastrointestinal diseases.
why_this_matters_source: Importance of indicator — VII. Fecal Coliforms (factsheet_text.txt)

name: Diatoms and Diatom Teratology
protocol_question: Scrape periphytic diatoms from 5 submerged stones into a sample vial for slide preparation.
citizen_question: Scrape periphytic diatoms from 5 submerged stones into a sample vial for slide preparation.
visual_anchor_guide: Scrape periphytic diatoms from submerged stones into sample vial. Clean with nitric acid and potassium dichromate. Prepare permanent slides using Naphrax®.
lab_guidance: Requires nitric acid / potassium dichromate oxidation, resin mounting (Naphrax®), and microscopic valve identification (~400 valves) under 1000x magnification (EN 13942).
citation: Schmeller, D., Calapez, A.R., Silva, J.P., Norte, A.C., Serra, S.R.Q., Dias, M., Silva, G.T., Bouchali, R., Loyau, A., Almeida, S.F.P., Schmitt, R., Chen, A., Ramos, J.A., Feio, M.J. (2026). OneAquaHealth Key Indicators Factsheets Collection. Zenodo. doi:10.5281/zenodo.20345207
why_this_matters: Certain diatom species can form harmful algal blooms (HABs) in freshwater environments. These blooms can produce toxins and/or deplete oxygen levels in the water, harm aquatic organisms, leading to fish kills and posing risks to human health through contaminated water or food consumption.
why_this_matters_source: Importance of indicator — I. Diatoms and diatom teratology (factsheet_text.txt)
